introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geology (0555), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2024. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FIVE questions: choosing TWO questions from Section A, TWO from Section B and question 7 in Section C. (Note: Question 7 is compulsory.)

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

regles_choix.texte: Question 7 is compulsory: every candidate answers it.

figures.legende: Figure 1. Map extract (hand-drawn geological map with strike and dip symbols 45 and 60; north arrow on the right).
Figure 2. Crystal model (a bipyramid with a four-sided equatorial section).

incertitudes: Aucun corrigé officiel : les réponses modèles sont rédigées d'après les notions classiques du programme O Level de Géologie ; elles sont à faire relire par un géologue avant mise en avant. Le sujet est une feuille à compléter (lignes pointillées) : les lignes ne sont pas reproduites.

Règles de choix : page de garde « Answer FIVE questions: choosing TWO questions from section A, TWO from section B and question 7 in Section C. (Note: Question 7 is compulsory) ». Codé : parmi 2 sur 3 pour SECTION A, parmi 2 sur 3 pour SECTION B, et une règle `consigne` pour SECTION C (question 7 obligatoire, toujours comptée).

Question 7(a) : le sujet dit « answer questions 7.(a) (i), (ii) and (iii) » mais imprime aussi (iv) ; les quatre parties sont transcrites (2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5). De même 7(b) annonce (i), (ii), (iii) et imprime (iv) (1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 5). 7(c) : 5 x 1 ; 7(d) : 1 + 1 + 3 ; total 20, conforme au sujet.

Question 7(a) : la carte est un croquis dessiné à la main, sans légende ni échelle ; le type de pli (plongeant, asymétrique, anticlinal ou synclinal), la position de l'axe et l'identification du motif « X » (bouchon volcanique) sont des LECTURES du dessin, non certifiées : l'ordre d'âge des couches n'est pas donné, donc la distinction anticlinal/synclinal est une hypothèse. Plusieurs réponses du jury peuvent être acceptables ; réponse « bouchon volcanique » à faire relire par un géologue.

Question 7(b) : la figure est une bipyramide dont la section médiane est lue comme carrée (système tétragonal, bipyramide tétragonale) ; une lecture orthorhombique (base losange) ne peut pas être exclue sur ce dessin à main levée. Minéral donné : zircon (valeur de cours).

Figures : figure 1 (page 6) et figure 2 (page 7) produites avec le skill reproduire-figure-sans-filigrane (régime B_cuit, filtre de niveaux, contrôle OCR OK, relues à l'oeil) ; les mentions « Figure 1. » / « Figure 2 » du sujet sont conservées dans l'image.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Study the map extract (Figure 1). Use it to answer questions 7. (a) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geology-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

(i) Identify ONE type of fold on the map. (2 marks)

(ii) Insert the fold axis of the fold you have identified. (1 mark)

(iii) State the symmetry of the fold in 7a) (i). (1 mark)

(iv) Identify the feature with X at the centre. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Type of fold (any one correctly identified).** The beds are bent into curved, tongue-shaped outcrops that close at one end, which shows that the folds are **plunging folds**. The dips on the two sides differ ($45^\circ$ on the north-west side, $60^\circ$ on the south-east side), so the fold is also **asymmetrical**. The tongue with the dashed pattern (marked +) is read as a plunging **anticline**, and the tongue of conglomerate between the limestone bands as a plunging **syncline**. Answer: *plunging asymmetrical anticline* (or syncline).

**(ii) Fold axis.** Draw a straight line along the **middle of the chosen fold**, joining the points of maximum curvature of the outcrops (the hinge line), running roughly north-east to south-west through the centre of the dashed tongue (anticline), and mark it with the anticline symbol (a line with a cross). The line must lie between the two limbs, not on a limb.

**(iii) Symmetry.** The fold is **asymmetrical**: the two limbs dip at different angles ($45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$), so the axial plane is inclined and the limbs are not mirror images.

**(iv) Feature with X.** The small circular outcrop of a different rock (with a conglomerate-type pattern) cutting across the folded beds is a **volcanic plug (volcanic neck)**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Study the crystal model (Figure 2). Use it to answer questions 7. b) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv).

![fig-2](gce-ol-geology-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_2.png)

(i) To which system does the crystal model belong? (1 mark)

(ii) State the crystal form shown by the model. (1 mark)

(iii) Name a mineral that crystallizes in this system. (1 mark)

(iv) Use letters O and P and label any TWO faces. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The model is a double pyramid whose middle section (the base common to both pyramids) is four-sided and square, so it belongs to the **tetragonal system**.

**(ii)** The crystal form is a **tetragonal bipyramid** (tetragonal dipyramid): eight triangular faces, four meeting at the top apex and four at the bottom apex.

**(iii)** A mineral that crystallizes in the tetragonal system: **zircon** (also acceptable: rutile, cassiterite, chalcopyrite, vesuvianite).

**(iv)** Label any two of the triangular faces on the drawing, for example write **O** on the upper front face (apex, left corner, centre corner) and **P** on the upper right face (apex, right corner, centre corner). Any two different faces, correctly lettered, earn the 2 marks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Describe basalts based on the following:

(i) Grain size ........ (1 mark)

(ii) Colour ........ (1 mark)

(iii) Minerals present ........ (1 mark)

(iv) Structure ........ (1 mark)

(v) Use ........ (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Grain size:** fine grained (the crystals are too small to see without a lens), because the lava cools quickly at the surface.

**(ii) Colour:** dark, black or dark grey.

**(iii) Minerals present:** calcium-rich **plagioclase feldspar** and **pyroxene** (augite), often with **olivine** and magnetite.

**(iv) Structure:** often **vesicular** (gas bubbles) or amygdaloidal (vesicles filled with minerals); it may also show columnar jointing.

**(v) Use:** crushed stone (aggregate) for roads, concrete and railway ballast; also building stone.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) List ONE diagnostic physical property of haematite. (1 mark)

(ii) How many cleavage planes are found in the mineral biotite? (1 mark)

(iii) Arrange the following minerals beginning from the softest to the hardest; Gypsum, Fluorite and Calcite. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Any one: **reddish-brown (red) streak**; metallic or earthy lustre, steel-grey to red-brown colour; high density (about 5.3); hardness about 5.5 to 6.5. The most diagnostic is its **red-brown streak**.

**(ii)** Biotite has **one** perfect cleavage plane (basal cleavage), which splits it into thin flexible sheets.

**(iii)** On Mohs' scale gypsum is 2, calcite is 3 and fluorite is 4. From softest to hardest: **Gypsum (2), Calcite (3), Fluorite (4)**.
